articles.title: There’s No End in Sight to Yemen’s Destructive War

articles.content_excerpt: Yet again, the world is failing to give Yemen the attention it deserves. Well over a month into the renewal of the war between Ansar Allah, known as the Huthis, and the internationally recognized government (IRG), there have already been thousands of military and civilian casualties on both sides. The humanitarian situation is disastrous, with famine threatening in some parts of the country. articles.author: Peter Dreier
articles.content_excerpt: Organizers like to say that all politics boils down to a battle between organized money and organized people. Candidates with the largest war chests tend to win, but contenders who refuse to take donations from corporate interests can prevail if their supporters are well-organized, inspired, and strategic. Likewise, big employers can spend huge sums on union busting, but employees can win union organizing drives if they know how to mobilize workers to stick together and not be intimidated. The same is true in baseball. articles.title: Vancouver Is in the Middle of a Socialist Surge
articles.author: James Adair
articles.content_excerpt: Vancouver’s contrasts are visible on its streets. Luxury cars cruise past some of North America’s worst homeless encampments. Last Saturday, October 17, the city produced a political contrast to match: after four years of a center-right city hall, its municipal council has transformed into one of the most left-wing in North America. The breakthrough comes alongside strong socialist showings in municipal elections around the world, from Zohran Mamdani’s win in New York to Die Linke’s recent state election victory in Berlin. The Coalition of Progressive Electors (COPE), a democratic socialist party, elected all twelve candidates it ran: four to council, four to school board, and four to park board. articles.content_excerpt: United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain is poised to win a second four-year term, with an overwhelming lead in member balloting for the union’s top officers. articles.content_excerpt: WHITING, IND.— Six and a half months after being locked out of his job as a British Petroleum (BP) operator, Jon is still showing up to picket shifts. I met him on the side of a road, the refinery spewing smoke behind him. For a while, unemployment benefits of around $ 335 a week helped ease the financial burden, he tells me, but those went away at the end of September when he hit the six-month mark. And now, BP is appealing the locked-out workers’ unemployment with the state of Indiana. It’s a move that could result in workers like Jon having to pay back the assistance they’ve already received. articles.title: Wall Street Is Getting Very Nervous About AI
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: For an industry that we’re told is central to our collective future, the artificial intelligence (AI) industry increasingly seems to be built on a combination of artificially inflated hopes and bad accounting. articles.title: Class Struggle in the Major Leagues
articles.content_excerpt: On December 1st, 2026, at 11:59 PM, the collective bargaining agreement between Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Major League Baseball Player’s Association (MLBPA) will expire. Within a minute of the expiration, MLB owners will institute a lock-out of players , even though it is the off-season. Their likenesses will be scrubbed from all public-facing MLB media; teams will no longer be able to communicate with players and vice-versa. This will lead to a stalemate: neither side will make concessions, each waiting until the start of “spring training”, the pre-season for MLB. It is at this point that the struggle begins in earnest, as delays threaten the loss of paychecks and game revenue. Public pressure will begin to mount on both sides. articles.title: Chris Wickham Revolutionized Our View of the Middle Ages
articles.author: Paolo Tedesco
articles.content_excerpt: With the passing of Chris Wickham earlier this month, we have lost the greatest medieval historian since Marc Bloch, and one of the most original Marxist historians ever. In his career, which spanned half a century, Wickham wrote more than twenty books and two hundred articles. In these works, he showed how the social and economic structures of Europe and the Mediterranean transformed in the period from 500 to 1500. Key factors in his analysis were the rise and fall of the state, the political and economic role of the landowning elites, and the protagonism of the peasants. His massive intellectual production revolutionized not only our idea of the Middle Ages but above all our understanding of how societies function and change across time.
